source.title: DSD$^2$: Can We Dodge Sparse Double Descent and Compress the Neural Network Worry-Free?

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. Some equations and figures are flattened by text extraction, so plotted values are not recoverable exactly.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests sparse double descent through iterative pruning of trained deep networks, rather than reproducing the original dense-model size sweep. It also tests whether distillation changes the pruning-performance curve.
record.gate_note: The study measures test accuracy as sparsity increases and reports outcomes for pruning, width/depth sweeps, noise levels, and regularization choices. The plotted curves usually have no exact numeric values in the text, so those rows use figure only. Epoch-wise double descent and varying training-set size are discussed or cited but not tested here; cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps model size by iterative magnitude pruning (sparse double descent) on ResNet-18 and VGG-like nets. It reports test accuracy curves across label-noise levels, depth, width, datasets and regularizers. This is a different method aimed at the model-wise double-descent question. It also tests whether regularizers, including knowledge distillation, remove the peak. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find SDD consistently under pruning on noisy CIFAR data, and that it grows more evident with depth and width; they argue it relates to parameter count. The noise correlation concerns where the best model lies (Light vs Sweet Phase), not whether SDD occurs. Knowledge distillation from a pruned or dense teacher removes SDD, while standard regularizers do not. Training-set activation entropy lets early stopping be re-enabled.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines iterative pruning and retraining of already-trained models, measuring performance against sparsity, and also sweeps architecture depth/width. It does not use the original dense-model-size, epoch, or sample-count sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with pruning sparsity, label-noise level, architecture depth and width, dataset, perturbation/reinitialization strategy, and whether the student uses knowledge distillation. For CIFAR-10, the reported best phase changes around the 12.5%-to-15% noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: The entropy of activation states stays flat in the interpolation regime and falls once the model enters the classical regime, which lets early stopping be re-enabled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set activation entropy marks the boundary of the interpolation regime during pruning.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI24 (paper states acceptance at the 38th Annual AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)
record.problems: Most curve values relevant to SDD are figure-only rather than tabulated. The direct evidence concerns pruning/sparsity sweeps, not the original dense model-size, epoch, or sample-size axes. Several reported results are explicitly dataset- and training-regime-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix repeats width/depth sweeps for additional CIFAR-10 noise levels in Figs. 9-14; these are not separately extracted because the main text describes the sweep patterns and the selected rows already capture the stated width/depth and noise-dependent outcomes. The regularization comparison in Fig. 6 is included, but its plotted values are figure-only.

untested.parts: The dense-width sweep as in the original, and whether the peak sits at the size that just fits the training set. Size is varied only by pruning.
All: no sweep over training-set size.
All: no effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Multiple or triple peaks; optimally tuned regularization (only a few fixed λ values were tried); a direct comparison of peak size across noise levels.

missing.what: Structured L1 filter pruning, VGG-like δ=1, CIFAR-10 ε=50%. Vanilla accuracy is non-monotonic across 512→32 filters (66.80, 67.10, 68.43, 66.88, 65.20); the KD student is monotonic (73.08→65.70).
The KD student varying depth and width on CIFAR-10 ε=50% gives monotonic curves (SDD dodged), while the vanilla model shows SDD.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is on the pruning (sparsity) axis, which is treated here as a proxy for model size. Nearly all curve values are figure-only. Rows were relinked: KD and regularizer rows to V6, noise-sweep rows to V1 only. The dense ImageNet points are references, not results.

versions.untested_parts: Tests pruning/sparsity sweeps and some width/depth configurations, not the original dense-model size sweep or the precise location of a peak at the size that just fits the training set.
No sweep over training epochs measuring test error.
No sweep over the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
Experiments are on deep neural networks; the paper does not test the general curve across model classes.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Varies label-noise levels and tests selected regularizers, but does not test multiple/triple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.
Does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether this makes the curve an ordinary U-shape.

relationships.condition: Vanilla-trained ResNet-18 and VGG-like (δ=5, γ=5) under iterative pruning on CIFAR-10/100 with injected noise (10–50%) and on CIFAR-100N; all perturbation schemes
relationships.reason: The authors report SDD (accuracy dips, then recovers as sparsity grows) in every one of these curves (R1–R10, R13, R16, R19, R22, R25, R28, R31, R32). Values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy dipped and then recovered as sparsity increased across every tested noisy-label curve and perturbation scheme.

relationships.condition: Datasets without injected noise: Flowers-102 (no augmentation) and ImageNet

relationships.display_finding: Flowers-102 showed no double descent despite a large generalization gap, while ImageNet accuracy declined beyond 50% sparsity, including from 69.28 to 67.50, which the authors attributed to underparameterization.

relation.reason: The study directly measures sparse double descent and compares architectures, noise conditions and regularization interventions.

tranche.reason: Iterative pruning and retraining test model-size nonmonotonicity using a different procedure from growing dense networks.

source_check.notes: Results concern the sparsity axis with retraining; they do not establish the original dense size-scaling curve. V6 absent states describe failed peak removal at tested strengths, not failure of optimally tuned regularization.

statements.correction: Sec. 3.6: shallow models show only sweet and collapsed phases; low-width models show no SDD. Appendix I.2: no double descent on Flowers-102 without augmentation despite overfitting. Appendix I.3: no SDD in the reported ImageNet configurations; authors attribute this to under-parametrization.
statements.problem: Absence on Flowers-102 and ImageNet is correctly reported. Shallow or narrow models retain the sweet and collapsed phases; describing them as lacking recovery misidentifies the missing phase.

statements.correction: Appendix D: SDD persists with AutoAugment/CutOut, dropout 0.5, L1 at 1e-5 and L2 at 1e-4; L2 at 1e-3 shifts SDD left. Disappearance under optimally tuned regularization is untested.
statements.problem: The reported persistence under tested regularizers is accurate, but its limits_scope label does not follow for V6's optimally tuned regularization clause; optimal tuning was not established.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla pruning sweeps on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 and the stated noise conditions
reader_labels.reason: The study reports SDD in the test-accuracy curves as sparsity increases (R1-R6, R13, R16, R19, R22, R25, R28, R31-R32). This is evidence on a pruning/sparsity path, not a direct reproduction of the dense size-growth claim.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: KD avoids SDD in the reported CIFAR sweeps, while shallow/low-width models and Flowers-102 show no SDD; the ImageNet configurations also are described as showing none (R11-R12, R14-R15, R17-R18, R20-R21, R23-R24, R26-R27, R29-R30, R33-R47).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 noise levels in Table 12
reader_labels.reason: The reported best-accuracy phase shifts from Light Phase at ε = 10% and 12.5% to Sweet Phase at ε = 15%, 17.5%, 20%, and 50%, showing an association between label-noise level and the location of the best point (R54-R59).
